title: Security-relevant events generated by system services shall be logged where requ…
text: Security-relevant events generated by system services shall be logged where required to detect or investigate activity that could affect WSCA security.

title: System services and associated components shall be regularly assessed for vulner…
text: System services and associated components shall be regularly assessed for vulnerabilities and security updates shall be applied where required.

title: The operating system shall continuously monitor system services for security-rel…
text: The operating system shall continuously monitor system services for security-relevant anomalies, including unexpected service behaviour, unauthorised configuration changes, suspicious process activity, and indicators of compromise. Detected events shall be reported to the platform's security monitoring mechanisms for analysis, alerting, and incident response.

title: Only applications and utilities required for the operation, administration and m…
text: Only applications and utilities required for the operation, administration and maintenance of the WSCA environment shall be installed.

title: Execution of applications, scripts and utilities shall be restricted to authoris…
text: Execution of applications, scripts and utilities shall be restricted to authorised software. Application allow-listing or equivalent controls shall be applied where technically feasible.

title: Applications and utilities shall operate with the minimum privileges required fo…
text: Applications and utilities shall operate with the minimum privileges required for their intended functions.

title: Applications shall be isolated from the WSCA so that compromise of an applicatio…
text: Applications shall be isolated from the WSCA so that compromise of an application does not provide direct access to WSCA processes or resources.

title: Applications shall not be able to read, modify or execute WSCA memory unless exp…
text: Applications shall not be able to read, modify or execute WSCA memory unless explicitly authorised and required for operation.

title: Applications shall have access only to the system interfaces, files, devices and…
text: Applications shall have access only to the system interfaces, files, devices and services required for their intended functions.

title: Application binaries and security-relevant configuration shall be protected agai…
text: Application binaries and security-relevant configuration shall be protected against unauthorised modification.

title: Applications shall not establish network connections to untrusted networks unles…
text: Applications shall not establish network connections to untrusted networks unless explicitly required and authorised.

title: Applications shall be prevented from accessing WSCA security-relevant data unles…
text: Applications shall be prevented from accessing WSCA security-relevant data unless explicitly authorised.

title: Applications shall be configured and controlled to prevent exploitation of appli…
text: Applications shall be configured and controlled to prevent exploitation of application vulnerabilities from resulting in unauthorised privilege escalation affecting the WSCA.

title: Security-relevant application events that could indicate an attempt to compromis…
text: Security-relevant application events that could indicate an attempt to compromise the WSCA environment shall be logged where appropriate.

title: Applications installed on the platform shall be subject to vulnerability managem…
text: Applications installed on the platform shall be subject to vulnerability management. Unnecessary or unsupported applications shall be removed.

title: Applications in the WSCA environment shall be monitored for security-relevant an…
text: Applications in the WSCA environment shall be monitored for security-relevant anomalies, including unauthorised execution, unexpected application behaviour, suspicious process activity, and indicators of compromise. Detected events shall be reported to the platform's security monitoring mechanisms for analysis, alerting, and incident response.

title: Container images shall contain only the software, libraries and configuration re…
text: Container images shall contain only the software, libraries and configuration required for the intended WSCA function.

title: Only authorised container images and workloads shall be permitted to execute. Co…
text: Only authorised container images and workloads shall be permitted to execute. Container images shall originate from controlled and trusted sources.

title: Containers shall execute with the minimum privileges required. Privileged contai…
text: Containers shall execute with the minimum privileges required. Privileged containers shall not be used unless explicitly justified and authorised.

title: Containers shall be isolated from the host, other containers and unrelated proce…
text: Containers shall be isolated from the host, other containers and unrelated processes using the platform's available isolation mechanisms.

title: Container resource controls shall prevent one container from accessing or exhaus…
text: Container resource controls shall prevent one container from accessing or exhausting memory resources in a manner that could compromise the WSCA or the underlying platform.

title: Container access to host devices, filesystems, kernel interfaces and other host …
text: Container access to host devices, filesystems, kernel interfaces and other host resources shall be explicitly restricted. Unnecessary host mounts and device access shall not be permitted.

title: Container images, runtime components and container configuration shall be integr…
text: Container images, runtime components and container configuration shall be integrity-protected and changes shall be controlled.

title: Container network connectivity shall be restricted to the connections required f…
text: Container network connectivity shall be restricted to the connections required for WSCA operation. Unnecessary external network access shall be prevented.

title: Containers shall not have access to WSCA security-relevant data unless such acce…
text: Containers shall not have access to WSCA security-relevant data unless such access is explicitly required for the WSCA function.

title: Container configuration and runtime controls shall prevent container processes f…
text: Container configuration and runtime controls shall prevent container processes from escaping their isolation boundary or obtaining unauthorised host privileges.

title: Container runtime and security events relevant to the protection of the WSCA sha…
text: Container runtime and security events relevant to the protection of the WSCA shall be logged and made available for monitoring where appropriate.

title: Container images, runtimes and supporting components shall be regularly assessed…
text: Container images, runtimes and supporting components shall be regularly assessed for vulnerabilities. Vulnerable or unsupported images and components shall be updated or removed.

title: The container runtime and isolation mechanisms shall be monitored for security-r…
text: The container runtime and isolation mechanisms shall be monitored for security-relevant anomalies, including unauthorised container creation or modification, attempted isolation-boundary violations, unexpected resource access, and suspicious workload behaviour. Detected events shall be reported to the platform's security monitoring mechanisms for analysis, alerting, and incident response.

title: The WSCA execution environment shall contain only the runtime components, librar…
text: The WSCA execution environment shall contain only the runtime components, libraries, configuration and supporting functionality required by the WSCA.

title: The WSCA shall be isolated from unrelated applications, services and processes s…
text: The WSCA shall be isolated from unrelated applications, services and processes such that compromise of another component does not provide direct access to the WSCA.

title: The WSCA execution environment shall enforce memory protection mechanisms preven…
text: The WSCA execution environment shall enforce memory protection mechanisms preventing unauthorised access to WSCA memory and security-relevant runtime data.

title: The WSCA shall have access only to the platform interfaces, devices, files and s…
text: The WSCA shall have access only to the platform interfaces, devices, files and services required for its specified operation.

title: WSCA binaries, libraries and security-relevant configuration shall be protected …
text: WSCA binaries, libraries and security-relevant configuration shall be protected against unauthorised modification.

title: Network communication from the WSCA shall be restricted to explicitly authorised…
text: Network communication from the WSCA shall be restricted to explicitly authorised endpoints and protocols required for its operation.

title: Security-relevant WSCA data shall be protected against unauthorised disclosure, …
text: Security-relevant WSCA data shall be protected against unauthorised disclosure, modification and deletion by the underlying platform and other processes.

title: The execution environment shall prevent the WSCA or its supporting components fr…
text: The execution environment shall prevent the WSCA or its supporting components from obtaining privileges beyond those required for their specified functions.

title: Security-relevant events affecting the WSCA execution environment shall be logge…
text: Security-relevant events affecting the WSCA execution environment shall be logged where necessary to support detection and investigation of security events.

title: All runtime components, libraries and supporting software on which the WSCA depe…
text: All runtime components, libraries and supporting software on which the WSCA depends shall be subject to vulnerability management and security-update processes.

title: The WSCA execution environment shall be continuously monitored for security-rele…
text: The WSCA execution environment shall be continuously monitored for security-relevant anomalies, including unauthorised changes to runtime components or configuration, unexpected WSCA behaviour, suspicious resource access, and indicators of compromise. Detected events shall be reported to the platform's security monitoring mechanisms for analysis, alerting, and incident response.

title: Only authorised WSCA binaries, libraries and supporting components shall be perm…
text: Only authorised WSCA binaries, libraries and supporting components shall be permitted to execute within the WSCA execution environment.

title: The WSCA shall execute with the minimum operating system and platform privileges…
text: The WSCA shall execute with the minimum operating system and platform privileges required to perform its specified security functions.

title: Audit Data Generation
text: FAU_GEN.1.1: The TSF shall generate an audit record of the following auditable events: a) TOE start-up and shutdown; b) All auditable events for the not specified level of audit; c) each signing operation, including the wallet user identifier; d) authentication failure; e) wallet instance and user lifecycle events (registration, suspension, deprovisioning); f) administrative and management operations (FMT_SMF.1); and g) all self-test results (FPT_TST.1) and secure initialization (FPT_INI.1). h) failures listed in FPT_FLS.1 and FPT_RCV.4. i) warning that audit trail is near full capacity (FAU_STG_EXT.3) j) failing checks related to transaction-bound authentication evidence (FIA_UAE_EXT.1) k) failure of establishing or detected attacks on a secure or trusted channel (FTP_PRO.3/* and FPT_ITC.1/*) l) failure of identification or authentication. m)detection of integrity or authenticity errors in stored user data. n) migration of user key bindings from one wallet user to another by the Wallet Provider o) [assignment: other specifically defined auditable events]. FAU_GEN.1.2: The TSF shall record within the audit data at least the following information: a) Date and time of the auditable event, type of event, subject identity (if applicable), and the outcome (success or failure) of the event; b) For each auditable event type, based on the auditable event definitions of the functional components included in the PP, PP-Module, functional package or ST, [assignment: other audit relevant information].

title: User identity association
text: FAU_GEN.2.1: For audit events resulting from actions of identified users, the TSF shall be able to associate each auditable event with the identity of the user that caused the event.

title: Audit review
text: FAU_SAR.1.1: The TSF shall provide Wallet Provider with the capability to read [assignment: list of audit information] from the audit data. FAU_SAR.1.2: The TSF shall provide the audit data in a manner suitable for the user to interpret the information.

title: Protected Audit Event Storage
text: FAU_STG_EXT.1.1: The TSF shall be able to transmit the generated audit data to an external IT entity. FAU_STG_EXT.1.2: The TSF shall be able to store generated audit data on the TOE itself. FAU_STG_EXT.1.3: The TSF shall maintain a [selection: log file, database, buffer, [assignment: other local logging method]] of audit records in the event that an interruption of communication with the remote audit server occurs. FAU_STG_EXT.1.4: The TSF shall be able to store [selection: persistent, non-persistent] audit records locally with a minimum storage size of [assignment: number of records and/or file/buffer size(s)]. FAU_STG_EXT.1.5: The TSF shall reject remote API requests from Wallet Instances when the local storage space for audit data is full. FAU_STG_EXT.1.6: The TSF shall ensure the authenticity and integrity of the audit data when stored on an external IT entity or the TOE itself with cryptographic means.

title: Counting Lost Audit Data
text: FAU_STG_EXT.2.1: The TSF shall provide information about the number of dropped audit records the case where the local storage has been filled and the TSF takes one of the actions defined in FAU_STG_EXT.1.5.

title: Notification in Case of Possible Audit Data Loss
text: FAU_STG_EXT.3.1: The TSF shall generate a warning to inform [selection: Wallet Provider, Technical Administrator] before the audit trail exceeds the local audit trail storage capacity.

title: Enforced proof of origin
text: FCO_NRO.2.1: The TSF shall enforce the generation of evidence of origin for transmitted API requests from the Wallet Instance handled by the TOE at all times. FCO_NRO.2.2: The TSF shall be able to relate the Wallet Instance identifier of the originator of the information, and the transaction identifier, UTC timestamp of the information to which the evidence applies. FCO_NRO.2.3: The TSF shall provide a capability to verify the evidence of origin of information to the Wallet Provider given the corresponding audit record is retained by the audit log server.

title: Enforced proof of receipt
text: FCO_NRR.2.1: The TSF shall enforce the generation of evidence of receipt for received API requests from the Wallet Instance handled by the TOE at all times. FCO_NRR.2.2: The TSF shall be able to relate the session identifier of the recipient of the information, and the Wallet Instance’s certificate, public key or thumbprint and the transaction identifier of the information to which the evidence applies. FCO_NRR.2.3: The TSF shall provide a capability to verify the evidence of receipt of information to the Wallet Provider given the corresponding audit record is retained by the audit log server.

text: FCS_CKM.2.1: The TSF shall distribute cryptographic keys in accordance with a specified cryptographic key distribution method [assignment: cryptographic key distribution method] that meets the following: [assignment: list of standards].

text: FCS_CKM.5.1: The TSF shall derive cryptographic keys [assignment: key type] from [assignment: input parameters] in accordance with a specified key derivation algorithm [assignment: key derivation algorithm] and specified cryptographic key sizes [assignment: list of key sizes] that meet the following: [assignment: list of standards].

text: FCS_CKM.6.1: The TSF shall destroy all TSF generated and/or maintained keys and key material, including per-key authorisation data when no longer needed, during revocation, deprovisioning, factory reset or authorized deletion is requested. FCS_CKM.6.2: The TSF shall destroy cryptographic keys and keying material specified by FCS_CKM.6.1 in accordance with a specified cryptographic key destruction method [assignment: cryptographic key destruction method] that meets the following: [assignment: list of standards].

text: FCS_COP.1.1: The TSF shall perform [assignment: list of cryptographic operations]

title: Access Control Policy
text: FDP_ACC.1.1/User_Creation: The TSF shall enforce the User Creation SFP on - Subject: Wallet Provider or Wallet Instance - Objects: Wallet User - Operations: Create new user The TOE creates a Wallet User with information provided by the subject.

title: Access control functions
text: FDP_ACF.1.1/User_Creation: The TSF shall enforce the User Creation SFP to objects based on the following: whether the subject is a Wallet Provider or Wallet Instance authorised to create a new Wallet User. FDP_ACF.1.2/User_Creation: The TSF shall enforce the following rules to determine if an operation among controlled subjects and controlled objects is allowed: only a Wallet Provider or Wallet Instance who has been authorised for creation of new users can carry out the operation. FDP_ACF.1.3/User_Creation: The TSF shall explicitly authorize access of subjects to objects based on the following additional rules: none. FDP_ACF.1.4/User_Creation: The TSF shall explicitly deny access of subjects to objects based on the following additional rules: [assignment: rules, based on security attributes, that explicitly deny access of subjects to objects].

title: Access Control Policy
text: FDP_ACC.1.1/Key_Creation: The TSF shall enforce the Key Creation SFP on - Subject: Wallet Instance - Objects: Asymmetric key pairs or symmetric keys - Operations: Create or delete new key or key pair Wallet Instances instructs the TOE to request the WSCD to generate/delete new keys/key pairs and assigns it to a Wallet User.

title: Access control functions
text: FDP_ACF.1.1/Key_Creation: The TSF shall enforce the Key Creation SFP to objects based on the following: the wallet instance is authorised to create, delete a symmetric key or asymmetric key pairs for a Wallet User. FDP_ACF.1.2/Key_Creation: The TSF shall enforce the following rules to determine if an operation among controlled subjects and controlled objects is allowed: the wallet instance requesting the creation of the key or key pair is authorised to carry out the operation. FDP_ACF.1.3/Key_Creation: The TSF shall explicitly authorize access of subjects to objects based on the following additional rules: none. FDP_ACF.1.4/Key_Creation: The TSF shall explicitly deny access of subjects to objects based on the following additional rules: [assignment: rules, based on security attributes, that explicitly deny access of subjects to objects].

title: Access Control Policy
text: FDP_ACC.1.1/Operation: The TSF shall enforce the Operation SFP on - Subject: Wallet User - Objects: Wallet User user-bound assets (including keys or key pairs) - Operations: (Per-key-authorized) Operations with Wallet User user-bound assets The TOE instructs the WSCD to carry out operations on and with the Wallet Users assets only where it corresponds to an assets within the WSCD-HSM that is bound to the identified Wallet User using per-key-authorization data provided by the wallet instance. - Subject: Wallet User - Objects: Wallet User user-bound assets (including keys or key pairs) - Operations: PIN reset The TOE instructs the WSCD to carry out PIN reset when the correct PUK was provided. - Subject: Wallet User - Objects: Wallet User user bound assets - Operation: Wallet User can clear or delete the Wallet User bound assets or migrate them to a different Wallet Instance. (This does not include the WSCD-stored plaintext private keys, only their reference, keyblobs and management).

title: Access control functions
text: FDP_ACF.1.1/Operation: The TSF shall enforce the Operation SFP to objects based on the following: whether the subject is a Wallet User or Wallet Provider authorised to carry out the operation or resets the PIN using the correct PUK. FDP_ACF.1.2/Operation: The TSF shall enforce the following rules to determine if an operation among controlled subjects and controlled objects is allowed: • only an authorized Wallet User is allowed to carry out operations using the keys or key pairs • a Wallet User is only allowed to carry out operations using their user-bound keys. • the authentication evidence is valid and bound to the current transaction. • the identifier of the Wallet User does match the user bound to the key or key pair • the Wallet User is active. • the integrity of all operation related assets was verified. • the Wallet Provider carrying out operations is authorized and authenticated. FDP_ACF.1.3/Operation: The TSF shall explicitly authorize access of subjects to objects based on the following additional rules: none. FDP_ACF.1.4/Operation: The TSF shall explicitly deny access of subjects to objects based on the following additional rules: any direct key access or key export requests for keys residing in the WSCD shall be denied [assignment: additional rules, based on security attributes, that explicitly deny access of subjects to objects].

title: Full residual information protection
text: FDP_RIP.2.1: The TSF shall ensure that any previous information content of a resource is made unavailable upon the deallocation of the resource from all objects.

title: Stored data integrity monitoring
text: FDP_SDI.1.1: The TSF shall monitor user data stored in containers controlled by the TSF or in its operative environment for integrity or authenticity errors on all objects, based on the following attributes: the integrity and authenticity check value bound to each stored object.

title: Stored data confidentiality
text: FDP_SDC.1.1: The TSF shall ensure the confidentiality of the following user data: session keys and WSCA-stored private keys while it is stored in the persistent memory (including the external database).

title: Authentication failure handling
text: FIA_AFL.1.1/Wallet: The TSF shall detect when [selection: [assignment: positive integer number], an administrator configurable positive integer within [assignment: range of acceptable values]] unsuccessful authentication attempts occur related to the authentication of the wallet user following FIA_UAE_EXT.1. FIA_AFL.1.2/Wallet: When the defined number of unsuccessful authentication attempts has been met, the TSF shall lock the wallet user and notify the wallet user via an out-of-band notification channel.

title: Authentication failure handling
text: FIA_AFL.1.1/Provider: The TSF shall detect when [selection: [assignment: positive integer number], an administrator configurable positive integer within [assignment: range of acceptable values]] unsuccessful authentication attempts occur related to the authentication of the wallet provider. FIA_AFL.1.2/Provider: When the defined number of unsuccessful authentication attempts has been met, the TSF shall [assignment: list of actions]

title: Authentication failure handling
text: FIA_AFL.1.1/Instance: The TSF shall detect when [selection: [assignment: positive integer number], an administrator configurable positive integer within [assignment: range of acceptable values]] unsuccessful authentication attempts occur related to the authentication of the wallet instance. FIA_AFL.1.2/Instance: When the defined number of unsuccessful authentication attempts has been met, the TSF shall [assignment: list of actions].

title: User attribute definition
text: FIA_ATD.1.1/Wallet: The TSF shall maintain the following list of security attributes belonging to individual users: a) wallet instance and wallet user identifier b) the registered Wallet Instance authentication credential, used both for authentication of the communication session and for verification of signatures over User Authentication Evidence c) the Authentication Reference Data against which the knowledge- and possession-based factor of the User Authentication Evidence is verified d) the binding records associating the wallet user with its wrapped key blobs, its attested key pairs and, where the WIA device-binding key pair is managed by the WSCA/WSCD, that key pair e) the per-key authorisation data associated with the wallet user for access to the WSCD-HSM, for the duration of the operation for which it was provided f) the authentication failure counter g) the wallet user status (active / suspended / deprovisioned) h) the integrity check value and version counter bound to the stored attributes of the wallet user i) [assignment: additional user security attributes].

title: User attribute definition
text: FIA_ATD.1.1/Provider: The TSF shall maintain the following list of security attributes belonging to individual users: a) the Wallet Provider identifier b) the Wallet Provider authentication reference data c) [assignment: additional provider security attributes]

title: User-subject binding
text: FIA_USB.1.1/Wallet: The TSF shall associate the following user security attributes with subjects acting on the behalf of that user: • the wallet instance and wallet user identifier • the wallet instance and wallet user authentication data • the wallet user status defined in FIA_ATD.1/Wallet • the binding records in FIA_ATD.1.1/Wallet • the per-key authorisation data in FIA_ATD.1.1/Wallet • [assignment: list of user security attributes] FIA_USB.1.2/Wallet: The TSF shall enforce the following rules on the initial association of user security attributes with subjects acting on the behalf of users: • the wallet instance identifier and the registered Wallet Instance authentication credential shall be associated only after successful identification in accordance with FIA_UID.2 and successful establishment of a trusted channel in accordance with FTP_PRO.2/Wallet • the wallet user identifier, the wallet user status, the binding records and the per-key authorisation data shall be associated only after successful verification of authentication evidence in accordance with FIA_UAE_EXT.1 against the Authentication Reference Data registered for that wallet user • only the attributes of the wallet user for whom the identified wallet instance is registered shall be associated • only the binding records and per-key authorisation data for the keys bound to that wallet user shall be associated • no attribute shall be associated where the wallet user status is other than active • no attribute shall be associated where an integrity or authenticity error has been detected in accordance with FDP_SDI.1 on the stored attributes concerned • [assignment: rules for the initial association of attributes] FIA_USB.1.3/Wallet: The TSF shall enforce the following rules governing changes to the user security attributes associated with subjects acting on the behalf of users: • the attributes associated under FIA_USB.1.2/Wallet • shall remain associated only for the operation for which the authentication evidence was verified, and shall be dissociated on completion of that operation or on expiry of the validity window of that evidence, whichever occurs first; • no associated attribute shall be modified at the request of the subject; • the authentication failure counter may change as a result of FIA_AFL.1; • a change of the wallet user status to suspended or deprovisioned shall take effect immediately and shall cause dissociation of all attributes associated with subjects acting on behalf of that wallet user; • a change to the binding records or to the per-key authorisation data shall take effect on the next association only. • [assignment: rules for the changing of attributes].

title: User-subject binding
text: FIA_USB.1.1/Provider: The TSF shall associate the following user security attributes with subjects acting on the behalf of that user: • the wallet provider identifier • the wallet provider authentication data • [assignment: list of user security attributes] FIA_USB.1.2/Provider: The TSF shall enforce the following rules on the initial association of user security attributes with subjects acting on the behalf of users: • attributes shall be associated only after successful identification in accordance with FIA_UID.2 and successful establishment of a trusted channel in accordance with FTP_PRO.2/Provider. • only the attributes of the Wallet Provider identified by the presented credential shall be associated; • only the role and the management functions for which that Wallet Provider is authorised shall be associated. FIA_USB.1.3/Provider: The TSF shall enforce the following rules governing changes to the user security attributes associated with subjects acting on the behalf of users: • no associated attribute shall change for the duration of the association; • revocation or modification of the Wallet Provider authentication reference data shall cause dissociation of all attributes associated with subjects acting on its behalf; • a change to the role or to the permitted management functions shall take effect on the next association only

title: User authentication before any action
text: FIA_UAU.2.1: The TSF shall require each user to be successfully authenticated before allowing any other TSF mediated actions on behalf of that user.

title: Re-authenticating
text: FIA_UAU.6.1: The TSF shall re-authenticate the user under the conditions before each signing request and for each credential management operation.

title: User identification before any action
text: FIA_UID.2.1: The TSF shall require each user to be successfully identified before allowing any TSF-mediated actions on behalf of that user.

title: Transaction-bound authentication evidence
text: FIA_UAE_EXT.1.1: The TSF shall generate, for each request to perform an operation in [assignment: list of operations requiring authentication evidence], a challenge with a minimum of 128 bits of entropy obtained from a random bit generation function meeting FCS_RBG.1. FIA_UAE_EXT.1.2: The TSF shall construct, for each challenge, a transaction context comprising the challenge, the identity of the user, the requested operation, and the wallet user identifier and [assignment: other transaction attributes] and shall associate that transaction context with the communication session on which the request was received. FIA_UAE_EXT.1.3: The TSF shall require that authentication evidence cryptographically bound to the transaction context of the requested operation be presented before the TSF performs any operation in operations defined in FIA_UAE_EXT.1.1. FIA_UAE_EXT.1.4: The TSF shall verify presented authentication evidence against the authentication reference data associated with the identified user and shall verify that the evidence demonstrates that each authentication factor in a) the possession-based factor of the wallet user and b) the knowledge-based factor derived from the PIN was verified. FIA_UAE_EXT.1.5: The TSF shall verify that presented authentication evidence was received no more than [assignment: validity period] after the corresponding challenge was issued. FIA_UAE_EXT.1.6: The TSF shall deny the requested operation if any verification required by FIA_UAE_EXT.1.3, FIA_UAE_EXT.1.4 or FIA_UAE_EXT.1.5 fails.

title: Single-use enforcement for authentication evidence
text: FIA_UAE_EXT.2.1: The TSF shall maintain a nonce registry covering all transaction identifiers issued and all evidence received within the validity window defined in FIA_UAE_EXT.1.5. FIA_UAE_EXT.2.2: The TSF shall deny the requested operation if the presented authentication evidence refers to a challenge that was not issued by the TSF, that has already been used in successful verification, or whose validity period has expired.

title: Security roles
text: FMT_SMR.1.1: The TSF shall maintain the roles • Wallet User • Wallet Instance • Wallet Provider • [assignment: additional authorized identified roles]. FMT_SMR.1.2: The TSF shall be able to associate users with roles.

title: Specification of Management Functions
text: FMT_SMF.1.1: The TSF shall be capable of performing the following management functions: • For the Wallet Provider: o TOE unique self-identification of version and configuration o TOE maintenance o Audit data review o Factory Reset o Deletion or reset of user authentication data o [assignment: list of management functions to be provided by the TSF]. • For the Wallet User: o Modifying user authentication data o PIN reset using PUK o Wallet Instance Migration

title: Management of security attributes
text: FMT_MSA.1.1/User_Creation: The TSF shall enforce the User Creation SFP to restrict the ability to modify the security attributes that are Wallet User related as defined in FIA_USB.1/Wallet to the Wallet Provider or Wallet Instance.

title: Static attribute initialization
text: FMT_MSA.3.1/User_Creation: The TSF shall enforce the User Creation SFP to provide restrictive default values for security attributes that are used to enforce the SFP. FMT_MSA.3.2/User_Creation: The TSF shall allow the Wallet Provider or Wallet Instance to specify alternative initial values to override the default values when an object or information is created.

title: Management of security attributes
text: FMT_MSA.1.1/Key_Management: The TSF shall enforce the Key Management SFP to restrict the ability to modify, delete the security attributes Wallet User keys related attributes as defined in FIA_USB.1/Wallet to the Wallet Instance or Wallet Provider (deletion only).

title: Static attribute initialization
text: FMT_MSA.3.1/Key_Management: The TSF shall enforce the Key Management SFP to provide restrictive default values for security attributes that are used to enforce the SFP. FMT_MSA.3.2/Key_Management: The TSF shall allow the Wallet Instance to specify alternative initial values to override the default values when an object or information is created.

title: Management of security attributes
text: FMT_MSA.1.1/Operation: The TSF shall enforce the Operation SFP to restrict the ability to query the security attributes Wallet User keys related attributes as defined in FIA_USB.1/Wallet to the Wallet User.

title: Secure security attributes
text: FMT_MSA.2.1: The TSF shall ensure that only secure values are accepted for attributes defined in FIA_USB.1/Wallet and FIA_USB.1/Provider.

title: Management of TSF data
text: FMT_MTD.1.1/Provider: The TSF shall restrict the ability to modify the Wallet Provider and WSCD authentication data to Wallet Provider.

title: Management of TSF data
text: FMT_MTD.1.1/Provider: The TSF shall restrict the ability to modify the their Wallet User authentication data to an authenticated Wallet User. However, delete and clear are available for the Wallet Provider.

title: Management of TSF data
text: FMT_MTD.1.1/Provider: The TSF shall restrict the ability to modify the their Wallet Instance authentication data to an authenticated Wallet Instance. However, delete and clear are available for the Wallet Provider.

section: 6.7 Class FPT — Protection of the TSF
title: Failure with preservation of secure state
text: FPT_FLS.1.1: The TSF shall preserve a secure state when the following types of failures occur: WSCD-HSM connection failure; credential store integrity check failure; audit log unavailability; [assignment: additional types of failures in the TSF].

section: 6.7 Class FPT — Protection of the TSF
title: Inter-TSF confidentiality during transmission
text: FPT_ITC.1.1: The TSF shall protect all TSF data transmitted from the TSF to another trusted IT product the WSCD-HSM from unauthorized disclosure during transmission.

section: 6.7 Class FPT — Protection of the TSF
title: Inter-TSF detection of modification
text: FPT_ITI.1.1: The TSF shall provide the capability to detect modification of all TSF data during transmission between the TSF and another trusted IT product the WSCD-HSM within the following metric: [assignment: a defined modification metric]. FPT_ITI.1.2: The TSF shall provide the capability to verify the integrity of all TSF data transmitted between the TSF and another trusted IT product the WSCD-HSM and perform [assignment: action to be taken] if modifications are detected.

section: 6.7 Class FPT — Protection of the TSF
title: Function recovery
text: FPT_RCV.4.1: The TSF shall ensure that all credential management and HSM operations [assignment: additional list of functions and failure scenarios] have the property that the function either completes successfully, or for the indicated failure scenarios, recovers to a consistent and secure state.

section: 6.7 Class FPT — Protection of the TSF
title: TSF self-testing
text: FPT_TST.1.1: The TSF shall run a suite of the following self-tests during initial start-up, periodically during normal operation, at the request of the authorized user to demonstrate the correct operation of correct operation of cryptographic libraries if applicable; WSCD-HSM connectivity and authentication; credential store integrity; audit log availability; and correct operation of the transaction identifier registry [assignment: other parts of the TSF]: [assignment: list of self-tests run by the TSF]. FPT_TST.1.2: The TSF shall provide authorized users with the capability to verify the integrity of [selection: [assignment: parts of TSF data], TSF data]. FPT_TST.1.3: The TSF shall provide authorized users with the capability to verify the integrity of [selection: [assignment: parts of TSF], TSF].

section: 6.7 Class FPT — Protection of the TSF
title: TSF initalization
text: FPT_INI.1.1: The TOE shall provide an initialization function which is self-protected for integrity and authenticity. FPT_INI.1.2: The TOE initialization function shall ensure that certain properties hold on certain elements immediately before establishing the TSF in a secure initial state, as specified in [table: ID 1 – Properties: integrity – Elements: Software binary, configuration; ID 2 – Properties: [assignment: property, for instance authenticity, integrity, correct version] – Elements: [assignment: list of TSF/user firmware, software or data]] FPT_INI.1.3: The TOE initialization function shall detect and respond to errors and failures during initialization such that the TOE: is halted. FPT_INI.1.4: The TOE initialization function shall only interact with the TSF in a restrictive way that allows for the verification of the properties and elements stated in FPT_INI.1.2 during initialization.

title: The product context shall be identified and documented, covering the product's i…
text: The product context shall be identified and documented, covering the product's intended purpose and reasonably foreseeable use (IPRFU), its functions, its operational environment, an architectural overview, a description of its users including their experience level and security-relevant objectives, and where relevant and useful: general product insights from the market segments involved, including market expectations.

title: Where the product includes remote data processing solutions (RDPS), the RDPS sha…
text: Where the product includes remote data processing solutions (RDPS), the RDPS shall be considered to be included in the product context.

title: A documented procedure shall be maintained for establishing and updating the pro…
text: A documented procedure shall be maintained for establishing and updating the product context, including defined triggers for re-evaluation when the application, its RDPS, or its operational environment changes.

title: The cybersecurity risk acceptance criteria shall be established. At minimum, the…
text: The cybersecurity risk acceptance criteria shall be established. At minimum, the criteria shall account for the product context, regulatory factors, supply chain aspects, the nature of risks, the current state of the art, and user needs.

title: When conducting a product cybersecurity risk assessment, all cybersecurity asset…
text: When conducting a product cybersecurity risk assessment, all cybersecurity assets relevant to the product shall be identified, and it shall be determined which cybersecurity properties (confidentiality, integrity, availability, authenticity, and others as applicable) need to be ensured for each. This identification shall be grounded in the product context established under section 5.2, and the resulting asset list with associated cybersecurity properties shall be included in the product's technical documentation. The asset scope is broad and shall consider data assets (e.g. credentials, keys, personal data, configuration data, safety signals, firmware images, logs), functional assets, hardware and software components and interfaces, user-objective assets (health, safety, privacy, availability), and environmental assets (adjacent networks, third parties, public interest, and assets involved in RDPS).

title: In case the application employs AI models, AI-specific assets shall be included …
text: In case the application employs AI models, AI-specific assets shall be included in the considerations to identify cybersecurity assets.

title: Drawing on the established product context, product cybersecurity risks shall be…
text: Drawing on the established product context, product cybersecurity risks shall be identified. Each identified risk shall specify which asset(s) are targeted, which cybersecurity objective(s) of those assets may be compromised, and the cause of that potential compromise.

title: Where publicly known vulnerabilities exist that are relevant to the product's as…
text: Where publicly known vulnerabilities exist that are relevant to the product's assets and their associated cybersecurity properties, those publicly known vulnerabilities shall be identified. This obligation is conditional on the availability of such information.

title: A documented threat modelling procedure specific to mobile applications shall be…
text: A documented threat modelling procedure specific to mobile applications shall be established and maintained, defining the methodology to be applied (e.g., STRIDE, PASTA, attack trees), the threat catalogues to use, the roles responsible for conducting threat modelling, and the trigger conditions under which threat modelling shall be performed or repeated (e.g., new feature introduction, platform OS update, third-party SDK integration).

title: For each product cybersecurity risk identified in accordance with 5.5, the likel…
text: For each product cybersecurity risk identified in accordance with 5.5, the likelihood of the associated cybersecurity incident occurring shall be estimated.

title: For each product cybersecurity risk identified in accordance with 5.5, the sever…
text: For each product cybersecurity risk identified in accordance with 5.5, the severity of impact of the associated cybersecurity incident shall be estimated.

title: For each product cybersecurity risk identified in accordance with 5.5, the cyber…
text: For each product cybersecurity risk identified in accordance with 5.5, the cybersecurity incident scenario in which that risk could materialize shall be documented.

title: A repeatable risk analysis methodology for cybersecurity risks shall be defined …
text: A repeatable risk analysis methodology for cybersecurity risks shall be defined and documented, specifying the rating scale, criteria, and scoring rationale to be applied consistently across all risk assessments.

title: The rationale and evidence supporting each likelihood and severity result shall …
text: The rationale and evidence supporting each likelihood and severity result shall be documented, enabling independent review and auditability of the risk analysis.
